title: Kernel-normalized determinant maps for surjective two-term quasi-isomorphisms
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. A finite projective $R$-module means a direct summand of a finite free module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. For such a module $V$, write $\det_R(V)$ for its determinant module: on each constant-rank locus of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-pc-scheme] it is the top exterior power, with the transition maps induced by exterior powers [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra]; equivalently use finite free localizations as in [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover] and their usual change-of-basis determinant maps. Put $D(P)=\det_R(P^0)\otimes_R\det_R(P^{-1})^\vee$ for a cochain complex $P=[P^{-1}\xrightarrow{d_P}P^0]$ of finite projective modules, zero in other degrees; here $V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_R(V,R)$. For a degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphism $a:P\to Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], let $N^i=\ker(a^i)$ with the induced differential. Then $N^{-1},N^0$ are finite projective and $d_N:N^{-1}\to N^0$ is an isomorphism. Let $\gamma^i:\det_R(N^i)\otimes_R\det_R(Q^i)\xrightarrow{\sim}\det_R(P^i)$ be the short-exact-sequence map: wedge a basis of the kernel first and lifts of a basis of the quotient second, locally, independently of the chosen lifts. Let $\Gamma_a:D(Q)\otimes_R D(N)\xrightarrow{\sim}D(P)$ be the map obtained from $\gamma^0$ and the inverse dual of $\gamma^{-1}$, reordering ordinary tensor factors by the symmetry. The determinant $\delta_N=\det(d_N)$ is a trivialization of $D(N)$. Define $T_a:D(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}D(Q)$ by $\Gamma_a(x\otimes\delta_N)=T_a^{-1}(x)$. These explicitly defined maps have the following calculus: $T_{\mathrm{id}_P}=\mathrm{id}_{D(P)}$; if $a,b:P\to Q$ are degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphisms and $b^0-a^0=d_Qh$, $b^{-1}-a^{-1}=hd_P$ for an $R$-linear $h:P^0\to Q^{-1}$, then $T_a=T_b$; and for degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphisms $a:P\to Q$, $b:Q\to S$, one has $T_{ba}=T_b\circ T_a$.

proof.text: For the identity map the kernel is zero, $D(N)=R$ and $\delta_N=1$. The kernel-first wedge map of [lem-trf-projective-determinant-exact-sequence] has empty kernel wedge, so $\Gamma_{1}(x\otimes1)=x$ and $T_1=1$.

source.place: Tag 0FJI (section-determinants-complexes), identity case of the construction; Tag 0FJB (lemma-det-ses), empty kernel wedge.

proof.text: For homotopic $a,b$, [lem-trf-two-term-normalization-locality-equivariance] reduces equality of $T_a,T_b$ to each prime localization and identifies their constructions there, with finite free terms. Over that local ring [lem-trf-local-homotopy-unit-determinant-lift] supplies a chain automorphism $k$ with $ak=b$ and $D(k)=1$. Apply the equivariance formula in [lem-trf-two-term-normalization-locality-equivariance] with $a'=b$, $u=k$, $v=1$: $T_aD(k)=T_b$. This proves equality locally and hence globally.

source.place: Tag 0FJK (lemma-homotopic-surjections), localization reduction and automorphism square.

proof.text: For composition put $N=\ker a$, $M=\ker b$, $L=\ker(ba)$. The composite is surjective and induces composite cohomology isomorphisms, so [lem-trf-two-term-kernel-normalization] applies to all three maps. The restriction $a^i:L^i\to M^i$ has kernel $N^i$ and is onto: lift $m\in M^i$ through $a^i$; its lift lies in $L^i$ since $b^im=0$. It splits by [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. The quotient isomorphisms are $L/N\to M$, $[l]\mapsto a(l)$; $P/N\to Q$, $[p]\mapsto a(p)$; and $P/L\to S$, $[p]\mapsto ba(p)$. Their injectivity and surjectivity follow from these kernel checks and surjectivity of $a,ba$. They commute with differentials by the chain equations. The map $P/N\to P/L$ becomes $b:Q\to S$, since both send $[p]$ to $ba(p)$. Thus this is the required flag with finite projective terms.

source.place: Tag 0FJL (lemma-compose-surjections), kernel flag for the composite; explicit exactness and quotient identifications.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-acyclic-two-term-flag-determinants] to this flag. Under Step 4's quotient isomorphisms its three $G$ maps become $\Gamma_a,\Gamma_b,\Gamma_{ba}$: [lem-trf-projective-determinant-exact-sequence] sends kernel wedges and quotient lifts to the same ordered wedge on either side. For $c:L/N\xrightarrow{\sim}M$, $c^0d_{L/N}=d_Mc^{-1}$; a wedge $e$ and its differential image therefore go to $\det(c^{-1})e$ and $\det(d_M)\det(c^{-1})e$. Thus $D(c)\delta_{L/N}=\delta_M$. The differentials of $N,L$ are unchanged. Substitute $z_M=\delta_M$, $z_N=\delta_N$ in the two flag identities:
$$\Gamma_a(\Gamma_b(x\otimes\delta_M)\otimes\delta_N)=\Gamma_{ba}(x\otimes\delta_L).$$
By normalization the left side is $T_a^{-1}(T_b^{-1}(x))$ and the right side is $T_{ba}^{-1}(x)$. Taking inverses gives $T_{ba}=T_b\circ T_a$.

lean.statement: theorem surjective_two_term_determinant_calculus {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {P Q : TwoTermComplex R} (a : TwoTermMap P Q) [Module.Finite R P.neg] [Module.Projective R P.neg] [Module.Finite R P.zero] [Module.Projective R P.zero] [Module.Finite R Q.neg] [Module.Projective R Q.neg] [Module.Finite R Q.zero] [Module.Projective R Q.zero] (ha : a.DegreewiseSurjective) (hqa : a.QuasiIso) : Module.Finite R (LinearMap.ker (ModuleCat.Hom.hom a.neg)) ∧ Module.Projective R (LinearMap.ker (ModuleCat.Hom.hom a.neg)) ∧ Module.Finite R (LinearMap.ker (ModuleCat.Hom.hom a.zero)) ∧ Module.Projective R (LinearMap.ker (ModuleCat.Hom.hom a.zero)) ∧ Function.Bijective a.kernelDifferential ∧ kernelNormalizedDeterminantMap (TwoTermMap.id P) (TwoTermMap.id_degreewiseSurjective P) (TwoTermMap.id_quasiIso P) = LinearEquiv.refl (R := R) (twoTermDeterminant P) ∧ (∀ (a' : TwoTermMap P Q) (ha' : a'.DegreewiseSurjective) (hqa' : a'.QuasiIso) (h : (P.zero : Type v) →ₗ[R] (Q.neg : Type v)), ModuleCat.Hom.hom a'.zero - ModuleCat.Hom.hom a.zero = ModuleCat.Hom.hom Q.differential ∘ₗ h → ModuleCat.Hom.hom a'.neg - ModuleCat.Hom.hom a.neg = h ∘ₗ ModuleCat.Hom.hom P.differential → kernelNormalizedDeterminantMap a ha hqa = kernelNormalizedDeterminantMap a' ha' hqa') ∧ (∀ (S : TwoTermComplex R) [Module.Finite R S.neg] [Module.Projective R S.neg] [Module.Finite R S.zero] [Module.Projective R S.zero] (b : TwoTermMap Q S) (hb : b.DegreewiseSurjective) (hqb : b.QuasiIso), kernelNormalizedDeterminantMap (TwoTermMap.comp b a) (TwoTermMap.comp_degreewiseSurjective a b ha hb) (TwoTermMap.comp_quasiIso a b hqa hqb) = (kernelNormalizedDeterminantMap a ha hqa).trans (kernelNormalizedDeterminantMap b hb hqb))
